record.current_corrections: The blockade began on Monday 3 July and remained active on 4 July. A 6 July report describes completed lifting and freight passage, without naming the lifting day. The scoped endpoint is bounded to 4–6 July: a 1–3 calendar-day difference, not an exact three-day or 72-hour closure.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the July 2023 Yacuiba–Salvador Mazza protest obstruction, supported by active-blockade and completed freight-return reporting. Keep bridge/approach freight disruption and reported personal-movement effects. Return of trucks in both directions does not establish that every pedestrian was continuously blocked. Retain onset 3 July, still active 4 July, and endpoint bounded to 4–6 July, yielding one to three calendar days. The reported 19:00 clock lacks a named lifting day and cannot establish exactly three days or seventy-two hours. Retain Trade and protectionism / Trade and transport protests for bagayeros’ stated customs demands. Alleged improper seizures remain attributed, not independently adjudicated. El País quotes the protest leader. Tarija 200 credits Yacuiba Noticias and relays the consul through InfoPocitos; these credits are not extra independently inspected return reports. Retain unlocated Yacuiba–Salvador Mazza bridge/approach scope with null coordinates. No entire Bolivia–Argentina frontier or uniform pedestrian exclusion is mapped.
